title: Identity homotopy factor does not change the complex right-derived unit
statement: Let $C,D$ be abelian categories equipped with derived categories, assume $C$ has K-injective resolutions, and let $F:C\to D$ be additive [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Write $q_C$ for the quotient to the homotopy category, $Q_C$ for localization from complexes, $Q_C^h$ for localization from the homotopy category, and $\alpha_C:q_CQ_C^h\cong Q_C$ for the canonical comparison. Let $\beta:q_CF^h\cong F^\bullet q_D$ be the canonical factor comparison. For every complex $K$, the morphism $\alpha_D^{-1}(F^\bullet K);Q_D^h(\beta_K^{-1});u_F(q_CK);RF(\alpha_C(K))$ equals the canonical complex unit $u_F^Q(K):Q_D(F^\bullet K)\to RF(Q_CK)$.

source.place: definition-derived-functor, lines 5277-5295; canonical quotient-comparison specialization of the right-derived unit, as implemented by rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ.

proof.text: The inverse component of mapHomotopyCategoryFactors is identity by its quotient-lift construction. Its image under Qh is identity by functoriality. Deleting the identity factor leaves exactly the definition of rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ. This argument is made for abstract abelian categories and therefore need not unfold any sheaf-specific limit or colimit choices.

theorem rightDerivedComplexUnitNormalization
    {C D : Type*} [Category* C] [Category* D] [Abelian C] [Abelian D]
    [HasDerivedCategory C] [HasDerivedCategory D] [Abelian.HasKInjectiveResolutions C]
    (F : C ⥤ D) [F.Additive] (K : CochainComplex C ℤ) :
    (DerivedCategory.quotientCompQhIso D).inv.app _ ≫
        DerivedCategory.Qh.map ((F.mapHomotopyCategoryFactors (.up ℤ)).inv.app K) ≫
        F.rightDerivedFunctorUnit.app ((HomotopyCategory.quotient C (.up ℤ)).obj K) ≫
        F.rightDerivedFunctor.map ((DerivedCategory.quotientCompQhIso C).hom.app K) =
      F.rightDerivedFunctorUnitQ K
